# Pillar PEO Advisors

> Independent HR advisory firm for professional-services firms of 10–150 people, anywhere in the U.S., headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. Fixed-price HR audits, HR projects, fractional HR, and clean transitions into or out of a PEO. PEO brokerage is free to the client, with provider commission disclosed.

Pillar works with managing partners and practice administrators at law, CPA, engineering and architecture, medical and dental, RIA and nonprofit firms. Every engagement is priced before the work starts, and covers every state your people work in. Pillar sells no software and places no insurance.

## Services

- HR Audit (the Load Report) — fixed price set by headcount band and by how many states you employ in, quoted on the scope call.
- HR Projects — fixed price per project: handbook, FLSA review, I-9 and E-Verify, comp benchmarking, performance, manager training.
- Fractional HR — Advisor 8 hrs/mo, Partner 20 hrs/mo, Embedded 40 hrs/mo. Three-month minimum. Fixed monthly price.
- Transitions — fixed price: PEO exit, PEO switch, PEO implementation, HRIS migration, payroll switch.
- PEO brokerage — free to the client, provider commission disclosed in writing.

Prices are quoted before the work starts and are not published on the site.

## Compliance guides and tools

- [State Employer Guides](/resources/state-employer-guides): North Carolina and South Carolina only today. More states added as they are verified.
- [North Carolina Employer Guide 2026](/resources/state-employer-guides/north-carolina): HR rules organised by headcount. E-Verify at 25+ employees (NCGS 64-26); workers' compensation at 3+ employees.
- [South Carolina Employer Guide 2026](/resources/state-employer-guides/south-carolina): E-Verify for all employers within 3 business days of hire; workers' compensation at 4+ employees; 7 days' advance written notice of a change in wages; Pregnancy Accommodations Act at 15+ employees.
- [NC vs. SC Employment Law](/resources/nc-vs-sc-employment-law): Side-by-side table for firms with staff in both states.
- [Multi-State Employer Checklist](/resources/multi-state-employer-checklist): What to do the day you hire in a new state.
- [HR Audit Checklist](/resources/hr-audit-checklist): The nine areas and their checks, ungated, with a downloadable version.
- [E-Verify in North Carolina](/resources/e-verify-north-carolina): Required at 25 or more employees under NCGS 64-26.
- [E-Verify in South Carolina](/resources/e-verify-south-carolina): Required of all employers within 3 business days of hire.
- [NC Handbook Requirements](/resources/nc-handbook-requirements)
- [SC Handbook Requirements](/resources/sc-handbook-requirements)
- [Do We Need a PEO?](/resources/do-we-need-a-peo): Readiness self-assessment for first-time PEO buyers.
- [HR Risk Score](/tools/hr-risk-score): Nine-question assessment mapped to the nine audit areas. Score shown immediately.
- [PEO Cost Calculator](/tools/peo-cost-calculator): Estimate range with stated assumptions. No savings promised.

## How PEO pricing actually works

- [How PEO Pricing Actually Works](/resources/peo-pricing-explained): Hub for the PEO pricing cluster.
- [Why Your PEO Renewal Jumped](/resources/peo-honeymoon-pricing): Introductory pricing, repricing at renewal, switching-cost leverage.
- [The SUTA Line Nobody Checks](/resources/peo-suta-rates): Pooled unemployment rates, taxable wage base vs gross payroll, experience rating on entry and exit.
- [PEO Admin Fees](/resources/peo-admin-fees): Per employee per month vs percentage of payroll; gross vs taxable basis; unbundled quotes and sample invoices.
- [PEO Contract Terms](/resources/peo-contract-terms): Term, auto-renewal, notice windows, termination fees, plan-year exits.
- [When a PEO Is the Wrong Answer](/resources/when-a-peo-is-the-wrong-answer): Four cases where a PEO adds cost without removing work, with a labelled illustrative example.
- [The Free PEO Renewal Review](/resources/peo-renewal-review): Free renewal benchmark starting about 120 days out; provider commission disclosed.

## Editorial policy

Pillar is not a law firm and publishes no legal advice. Every state figure on this site carries a "Last verified" date and cites the statute or agency. Where a threshold has not been verified, the page says so rather than guessing. Pillar publishes no testimonials, client names or metrics it cannot evidence.
